related.title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027

cards.body: - Revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago - Data Center revenue of $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year ago - Vera Rubin NVL72, the most versatile and advanced computing platform ever built, has shipped NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively. GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.70 and $2.68, respectively. “Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.” In September 2026, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors approved an increase of $150 billion to the company’s share repurchase authorization, without expiration. During the third quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the form of shares repurchased and cash dividends. As of the end of the third quarter, the company had approximately $227.3 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization. NVIDIA will pay its next quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share on December 23, 2026, to all shareholders of record on December 2, 2026. related.title: Nvidia's Colette Kress tells Cramer: Employees and customers are not going anywhere

cards.body: Nvidia's customers and employees remain committed to the company despite last week's abrupt departure of longtime leader Jensen Huang. That's the message interim CEO Colette Kress conveyed exclusively to CNBC's Jim Cramer shortly after the AI chip giant delivered a quarterly beat and strong guidance. "[Hyperscalers] are the ones that are right now feverishly looking for more focus in terms of the compute that we have available," Kress said on "Mad Money." "This concept that anything is changing in terms of any of our types of customers — that is just not true. They are all continuing to be with us, and we have a very deep breath of different customers." Kress' comments came after Nvidia reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings and revenue and bumped up its fiscal 2028 revenue growth estimate to 75% from the previous 70%. It was the first earnings report since Huang's resignation as CEO amid a widening affair scandal. Shares rose nearly 4% in after-hours trading as the results helped ease concerns about the chipmaker's outlook following the leadership shake-up. Some on Wall Street have wondered whether Huang's departure would prompt certain Nvidia customers to lean harder into their in-house designed chips and/or competitors such as Advanced Micro Devices. During the "Mad Money" interview Tuesday evening, Kress emphasized that major customers have continued expressing interest in the company's products. "I have seen already with many of these [customers] contacting me and saying, 'Great to see everything intact. Great to see that there's more supply. I need more demand.'" Customer demand, however, wasn't the only issue facing Nvidia. Huang's departure has also raised questions about whether the chipmaker can retain the engineers and other employees who helped build its dominance in artificial intelligence. The co-founder was widely viewed as the driving force behind Nvidia's technology and corporate culture. Kress dismissed concerns about a potential employee exodus, stressing to Cramer that the workforce's longstanding commitment to the company is intact, and so is support from the leadership team. "The company has been built under the perspective that the employees look at Nvidia as their life work, and many of them have been here for many decades, working with us both from a technology standpoint or a business and operations perspective," she said. "We have high confidence that our employees are definitely still working, still working with us, and enjoy ... the work here at Nvidia," Kress told Cramer. related.title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now

cards.body: Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won’t stop. On Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company’s guidance. Nvidia had told Wall Street to expect $108 billion in revenue for its third quarter of fiscal 2027. Kress also projected an even bigger fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. She also said full-year revenue is on track to exceed expectations. “We are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base,” Kress said on the quarterly conference call on Tuesday. “Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.” The company also reminded investors that it was using some of its billions in cash to buy back shares. In September 2026, Nvidia increased its share buyback program by $150 billion. It spent $28.1 billion on its own shares during the quarter and still had another $227.3 billion remaining in the kitty for additional repurchases. Ironically, Nvidia could also benefit from the plunge in its share price following Huang’s resignation last week, should shares remain depressed over the longer term. The stock is down about 10% since his departure. Investors, however, celebrated Tuesday’s quarterly results, sending shares up about 4% in after-hours trading. Kress stressed that the company was in good shape now and for the foreseeable future, even without Huang at the helm. “We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress stressed. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.” She added that the company has secured memory and advanced packaging capacity and is working with its chip manufacturer, TSMC, to “narrow the supply and demand gaps.”

cards.body: Nvidia reported revenue up 103 percent over last year, beating expectations at $115.84 billion. However, the company reiterated that it has no plans to bring back founder Jensen Huang, who left this month amid numerous affairs. This quarter was the last with Huang at the helm. The company reported earnings of $2.68 per share, also above Wall Street expectations. Data center revenue was $107.6bn, up 110 percent year-over-year. Edge computing revenue hit $8.2bn, up 42 percent. Net profit hit $65.3bn, up 105 percent. Crucially, amid broader market uncertainty, interim CEO Colette Kress raised guidance by five percent, saying that Nvidia now expects 75 percent growth. The former CEO said that it was "business as usual at Nvidia.” She added: “Our leadership has stood up so strongly over the last week to support both what we are doing here at earnings, but also supporting all of our different employees around the world. “Remember, we have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap. And I think that’s important from a business perspective.” Unresolved questions still remain over whether Nvidia will continue to backstop deals with its customers, fund startups buying GPUs, and make large financial commitments to keep the AI economy going. The company said it is "not assuming any data center compute revenue from China in our outlook," but it faces investigations into its role in selling chips to Singapore that ended up in China. The company has denied any wrongdoing. Nvidia has faced mounting calls to reinstate Jensen Huang, who was fired after admitting an affair with an executive accused of funneling chips into China. Huang also had multiple affairs with Nvidia staffers. Board chair Harvey Jones pushed back on those calls, saying in the earnings call that Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” More in The Investment & Markets Channel - Episode 2027 Trends and Outlooks: Europe

headlines.body: A criminal investigation into Megaspeed has been confirmed by the United States Justice and Commerce Departments, with a joint statement saying that they will “bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred.” Authorities believe that Megaspeed is one of a raft of companies that may have circumvented export rules designed to limit the sale of advanced AI chips, like those built by Nvidia, to approved companies and countries. The company is at the heart of the recent Jensen Huang scandal, which saw him resign from the company last week . Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc) While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply market The state of China's decade-long semiconductor push Huawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fab China's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained Megaspeed was added to Nvidia's no-sell list in June 2025, the statement reveals, but a New York Times report claims that a Malaysian Megaspeed subsidiary continued to receive large shipments of Nvidia chips for a full eight months after that date. It's believed that Nvidia's export-controlled Blackwell and H200 chips were shipped to Speedmatrix, either via third parties or directly from Nvidia itself, before being handed off to China. Nvidia has argued that it was given Commerce Department permission to ship the components to Megaspeed. Notably, Nvidia continues to list Megaspeed as a cloud partner. The new criminal investigation follows a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed that first kicked off in 2024 over possible export violations. By May 2025, it had requested Nvidia's data relating to sales it made to Megaspeed, and by June, officials visited Megaspeed and even interviewed Alice Huang, the now-former executive who is allegedly a Chinese spy . Ms. Huang is also the woman that then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with before resigning his position earlier this month . Following that visit, the Justice Department took the lead in the investigation into Megaspeed. Joint Statement from Department of Commerce and Department of Justice on Megaspeed Investigation. https://t.co/aAdtN9aDfF November 17, 2026 Megaspeed has long been accused of being a front for an AI component smuggling operation. In October 2025, an investigation claimed that it had helped move around $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips into China by importing them and then re-exporting them to the country. Megaspeed says that it complies with all laws and that the woman at the center of the affair scandal, Ms. Huang, is no longer at the company. The Chinese government has also dismissed claims that she was a state spy. headlines.body: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country. China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia announced it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks. Nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff. The pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more important for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.” Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a company under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with new rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely. Investment bank Jefferies forecast that those rules might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year. Referencing the new export controls, Kress said that the backlog of demand for advanced chips like Vera Rubin means the rules would have no impact on the company’s top-line revenue. In the long term, the company may face the loss of potential customers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. Critics of Nvidia’s dependence on China claim that as much as 20% of its revenue comes from demand linked to the country — annual revenue at its Singapore subsidiary hit $104 billion in 2025 before Nvidia stopped disclosing those figures — but that’s clearly going to change. Even before Nvidia decided to stop shipping H200s, China had largely refused to accept their delivery. The government would prefer to generate demand for the country’s domestic chip industry, even if major AI compute users want the still-superior Nvidia equipment, according to Jacob Feldgoise, a researcher at Georgetown’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology. Meanwhile, Chinese frontier labs are finding ways to access Nvidia chips elsewhere. All of China’s leading AI models show evidence of having been trained on Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips that are prohibited from being exported to China. That training may have taken place at data centers outside of China, but sales to those facilities will be barred under the new rules. headlines.body: AI 추천 뉴스 네이버, 용접로봇 기업 투자…AX 영토 확장 금융·공공 이어 제조 AI로 美 패쓰로보틱스, 용접 자동화 록히드마틴 등이 주요 고객사 네이버, 지멘스·미스트랄AI 이어 피지컬 AI·해외 네트워크 확대 네이버가 용접 자동화 기술을 보유한 미국 피지컬 인공지능(AI) 기업에 투자했다. 금융·공공 분야에 집중해온 기업 간 거래(B2B) 인공지능 전환(AX) 사업을 제조업으로 확장하기 위한 행보다. 글로벌 제조업 현장에서 검증된 기술을 확보하는 동시에 향후 자사 AI 데이터센터 사업의 잠재 고객군을 넓히려는 전략으로 분석된다. ◇ 피지컬AI 기업에 첫 투자 17일 업계에 따르면 네이버의 투자 자회사인 네이버벤처스는 이달 초 미국의 패쓰로보틱스가 진행한 3억달러 규모 시리즈E 투자 라운드에 참여했다. 구체적인 투자 금액은 공개되지 않았다. 2018년 미국 오하이오주에서 설립된 패쓰로보틱스는 자체 AI 모델을 활용해 용접 공정을 자동화했다. 용접 부위와 금속의 변형 가능성을 스스로 인식·계산해 작업을 수행하는 기술을 보유했다. 용접 시스템과 로봇 플랫폼을 결합한 4족 보행 용접 로봇 ‘로브’도 개발했다. 대형 구조물의 용접 작업 현장까지 로봇이 직접 이동할 수 있어 작업 효율을 크게 높인다. 미국 최대 군함 건조업체인 HII와 방산업체 록히드마틴 등이 주요 고객사다. 특히 HII에는 지난 8월부터 7년간 6억달러 규모의 솔루션을 공급하기로 하는 등 미국 제조·방산업계에서 사업 기반을 넓히고 있다. 이번 투자는 네이버벤처스의 투자 영역을 피지컬AI로 확장했다는 점에서 의미가 있다는 평가를 받는다. 네이버벤처스는 네이버와 사업적 시너지를 낼 수 있는 성장 단계의 비상장 기업에 주로 투자했다. 그동안 AI 모델 개발사 앤트로픽과 음악 생성 AI 기업 수노 등 모델·솔루션 기업에 투자했지만, 피지컬AI 기업에 투자한 것은 이번이 처음이다. 지난해 6월 출범 이후 투자한 기업은 총 11개다. ◇ 제조·방산 등으로 AX 확장 네이버는 금융·공공 분야에 집중해온 B2B AX 사업을 제조업으로 확대하고 있다. 자체 AI 모델과 기업용 솔루션을 제조·방위산업·건설 등 산업 현장에 적용한다는 전략이다. 지난 6월 한국지멘스와 제조업 AX 공동 사업화에 나섰고, 7월에는 프랑스 AI 기업 미스트랄AI와 제조업 맞춤형 솔루션 개발에 협력하기로 했다. 이번 패쓰로보틱스 투자는 제조 현장에 적용할 피지컬 AI 기술과 글로벌 사업 네트워크를 확보까지 감안한 전략으로도 분석된다. 특히 AI팩토리 사업 고객사를 늘리는 데 도움이 될 것으로 전망된다. 네이버는 엔비디아, 브룩필드와 함께 2030년 초까지 1기가와트(GW) 규모의 AI 데이터센터 인프라를 구축한다. 글로벌 제조업의 자동화 수요가 커지는 점도 네이버가 관련 시장에 주목하는 배경이다. 산업연구원에 따르면 전 세계 산업 자동화 솔루션 시장은 지난해 9500만달러에서 2032년 18억8870만달러(약 2조5300억원)로 연평균 53.3% 성장할 전망이다. 네이버는 피지컬AI 분야 투자와 협력을 확대할 방침이다. 김남선 네이버 전략투자대표는 지난달 말 CNBC와의 인터뷰에서 “AI를 물리적 세계에 적용해 생산성을 높이는 분야의 잠재력이 크다”며 “다양한 분야의 AI 기업을 눈여겨보고 있다”고 말했다. 허진 기자 hjin@hankyung.com

stage1.korean_title: NVIDIA, 양자화 Qwen3.8 모델 'Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-QAD' 공개
stage1.korean_summary: NVIDIA가 Model Optimizer와 NeMo AutoModel을 활용해 양자화한 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-QAD 멀티모달 모델을 Hugging Face에 공개했다.

releases.body: Hugging Face 모델 신규 공개. pipeline: image-text-to-text · library: modelopt · tags: modelopt, safetensors, qwen4_exp, nvidia, ModelOpt, Qwen3.8, quantized, nvfp4, mxfp8, qad, image-text-to-text, conversational · downloads 0 · likes 42. README:  # Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-QAD This is an experimental mixed-precision QAD checkpoint of [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), exported after 100 optimizer updates using NVIDIA Model Optimizer and NeMo AutoModel with FSDP2. It contains the full multimodal model, including the frozen vision encoder, PLE n-gram embedding, and MTP module. Weight files occupy approximately 129.7 GB (120.8 GiB). **This checkpoint uses a more aggressive quantization recipe than [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4).** In addition to routed experts, it quantizes shared experts to NVFP4 and selected GDN, QSA, and indexer projections to MXFP8. The repository name's `-QAD` suffix identifies the training method; it does not mean the original NVFP4 recipe was kept unchanged. Task accuracy gains from QAD are not statistically established. Weight shards were consolidated for distribution. Every source file was verified against its export SHA256, and consolidated files passed a complete readback. releases.title: triton-inference-server/server Release 2.75.0 corresponding to NGC container 26.11

stage1.korean_title: Triton Inference Server 2.75.0 릴리스 (NGC 26.11)
stage1.korean_summary: Triton Inference Server가 PyTorch 백엔드 개선, 동적 배처 버그 수정, gRPC 성능 개선을 포함한 2.75.0 버전을 출시했다.

releases.body: Triton Inference Server The Triton Inference Server provides a cloud inferencing solution optimized for both CPUs and GPUs. The server provides an inference service via an HTTP or GRPC endpoint, allowing remote clients to request inferencing for any model being managed by the server. For edge deployments, Triton Server is also available as a shared library with an API that allows the full functionality of the server to be included directly in an application. New Features and Improvements PyTorch backend: Added AOTI BF16 input/output support. THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt is now included in the containers. Fixed a use-after-free in the dynamic batcher and a preserve_ordering completion-slot issue on response-cache hits. Prevented silent gRPC stream cancellations under backpressure. Bounded the decompressed HTTP inference response size in the client library. Perf Analyzer: Honored supplied output shapes, propagated the binary exit code, tagged the wheel as platform-specific, and limited profile-data export to the needed inputs and outputs. Python backend: Now logs when the backend stub exits on a crash signal. Known Issues The Triton TensorRT-LLM Backend container image is not included in this release. vLLM's v0 API and Ray are affected by vulnerabilities. Users should consider their own architecture and mitigation steps which may include but should not be limited to: Do not expose Ray executors and vLLM hosts to a network where any untrusted connections might reach the host. Ensure that only the other vLLM hosts are able to connect to the TCP port used for the XPUB socket. Note that the port used is random. When using Valgrind or other leak detection tools on AGX-Thor or DGX-Spark systems, you might see memory leaks attributed to NvRmGpuLibOpen. Valgrind or other memory leak detection tools may occasionally report leaks related to DCGM. These reports are intermittent and often disappear on retry.
